To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) can be differentiated from its mimics by the following features: 1. In the case of a well-differentiated HCC, a high Ki67 index, an intact bile duct system and a high degree of capillarization are typical. 2.
the diagnostic algorithm for HCC and its mimics should be based on the histologic and immunohistologic features, the clinical context, and the matrix diagnosis of the underlying liver tissue.
the diagnosis of hepatomas and their mimicking lesions is a complex task, which requires the integration of clinical, laboratory, radiological and histopathological findings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diagnosis of hepatomas and their mimickers.
the diagnosis of hepatobiliary tumors and the development of new diagnostic tools.
the development of a new diagnostic procedure for the diagnosis of HCC in liver biopsies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diagnostic algorithm for hepatocellular carcinogenesis is not yet complete.
the diagnosis of HCC is based on a combination of morphologic and immunohistologic criteria.
a biopsy is a useful diagnostic procedure for the detection of small HCCs in cirrhotic livers, but that it is of little value in the detection of small tumors in non-cirrhostic liver tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in most cases a definitive diagnosis of hepatocellar cancer can be made on the basis of liver tissue biopsy.
in most cases the diagnosis of hepatoblastoma and HCC can be achieved by a combined approach of morphologic, immunohistochemical, and molecular biological analysis of biopsy material.

the diagnostic procedure of hepatocellular carcinoma and its mimics should be adapted to the histologic diagnosis of the tumor bearing liver tissue, and that a combination of cyto-, histomorphologic and immunohistological analyses should be performed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diagnosis of HCC is a multidisciplinary process which includes morphologic, cyto- as well as histological and immunohistological analysis.
a biopsy is not always necessary for the diagnosis of HCC, but is necessary for the diagnosis and differential diagnosis of other hepatocellular lesions.
the diagnostic procedure of HCC should include a comprehensive histological workup of liver tissue.
